what: User decision Apr 21 2026 on derived-artifact resync (e.g. .ignore file): the CLI write path already live-resyncs via config.ts applySideEffects(). Question raised: who else listens for config.json changes? Answer: nobody does file-watching. Direct edits to .aide/config.json won't trigger resync. User's direction: centralize resync in one place — autoUpdateIfNeeded() on MCP server startup. All derived-artifact resyncs (currently just .ignore, more to come) should go through one shared function called both from config CLI writes AND from MCP startup drift-repair. Pattern: settings read on-demand (no resync needed) for hooks; settings that produce side-effects on disk (derived artifacts) resync via shared function on write + startup.
why: User's direction on how to handle config change propagation. Not obvious from code — centralizes what's currently two paths (CLI write + nothing) into two well-defined paths (CLI write + MCP startup). Avoids needing chokidar-style file watching for Phase 1.
